example: In `src/lib.rs`, a method `run` in `impl Thing` has selector `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`; a method `run` in `impl Trait for Thing` has selector `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`; and a method `read` declared in `trait Read` has selector `trait[Read]/fn[read]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`
rationale:
The example gives a concrete case in `src/lib.rs`. A method `run` in `impl Thing` has selector `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`. A method `run` in `impl Trait for Thing` has selector `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`. A method `read` declared in a trait has selector `trait[Read]/fn[read]`.

Two tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs` carry `{test}` references to the example.

- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` parses a source with the path `src/lib.rs`. That source has `struct Thing;`, `impl Thing { fn run() {} }`, `impl Trait for Thing { fn run() {} }` and `trait Trait { fn read(&self); ... }`.
  - It asserts that the outline contains `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]` and `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`.
  - It also asserts that `outline.resolve(selector)` returns a node whose selector equals the one asked for.
  - The two `run` methods get distinct selectors, one for the inherent impl and one for the trait impl.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` parses a similar source and asserts the same three selectors appear.

The trait in the tests is named `Trait`, not `Read`. That does not change the selector form `trait[Name]/fn[method]`. The tests check each expected outcome in the example, and I found no gap.

The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
